title: What Would It Take For Another Euro Crisis?

What Would It Take For Another Euro Crisis?

Cedric Gemehl

Gavekal Research | 21 Oct 2026

The widening of French sovereign debt spreads over the last month has prompted investors to consider the risk of another euro crisis and whether the mechanisms introduced since 2012 are robust enough to prevent one. For now, there are good reasons to think that French bond market tremors reflect a gradual repricing of France’s sovereign signature (see How Wide Can French Spreads Get?), rather than the start of a new crisis. But while the probability of a rerun looks low today, it could change over time. The useful exercise, therefore, is to identify the conditions that might increase that probability.A good starting point is to look back at the single currency’s difficult early life to establish what caused the euro crisis in the early 2010s and what eventually resolved it. The next step is to ask whether similar conditions exist today or could emerge in the future.
